```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
library(plotly)
```

## What this is about

I wanted to see how a car's power, weight and cylinder count together affect how far it goes on a gallon of fuel.

- Data: R's built-in `mtcars` dataset (32 cars, 1974 Motor Trend)
- Each point on the next slide is one car
- **Hover** over a point to see the car's name and details, **drag** to zoom, and **double-click** to reset

## Horsepower vs MPG

```{r plot, fig.width=10, fig.height=5}
cars <- mtcars
cars$name <- rownames(mtcars)
cars$cyl  <- factor(cars$cyl)

plot_ly(cars, x = ~hp, y = ~mpg, color = ~cyl, size = ~wt, sizes = c(8, 32),
        colors = c("#2a9d8f", "#e9c46a", "#e76f51"),
        type = "scatter", mode = "markers",
        marker = list(sizemode = "diameter", opacity = 0.8,
                      line = list(width = 1, color = "#ffffff")),
        text = ~paste0("<b>", name, "</b><br>MPG: ", mpg,
                       "<br>Horsepower: ", hp,
                       "<br>Weight: ", wt * 1000, " lbs"),
        hoverinfo = "text") %>%
  layout(xaxis = list(title = "Horsepower"),
         yaxis = list(title = "Miles per gallon"),
         legend = list(title = list(text = "<b>Cylinders</b>")))
```

<small>Bubble size shows the car's weight.</small>

## What the plot shows

- Fuel economy drops steeply as horsepower rises
- The 4-cylinder cars (green) form a clear cluster of light, efficient cars on the top left
- The 8-cylinder cars (orange) are heavier and sit at the bottom right
- A few cars, like the Maserati Bora, stand out with very high power and poor mileage
